checks_by_claim.source_location: PDF p.5 (10)–(13), pp.18–19 moment choices, p.20 actual use in Corollary 1.6
checks_by_claim.verification: The interval [M sqrt(n),M sqrt(n)] has one point; hence the printed endpoint-law domain admits only point masses, and may be empty for nonintegral offset. The actual outer-strip endpoint law has multiple positive reachable atoms for r>=1 with finite environment weights and is not in that domain. The spread-out rate witness below is explicitly for the minus-sign corrected box, not a counterexample on the literal singleton domain. For d=3 Gaussian disorder let pi in (0,1) be the positive-time return probability of the difference walk and beta^2=-log(pi)/90. Ten replicas give 45 pairs; Holder reduces the 10th moment to pair intersection moments with pi exp(45 beta^2)=sqrt(pi)<1. Thus P=p*>=10 and weak disorder follows from uniform L10 control and the usual zero-one law. A single path gives exponential q-moment growth when q>1+2log(6)/beta^2, so P is finite. Choose p=9/5, epsilon=1/22, n=2k^2 and the uniform law mu on even-parity sites in [0,k]^3; nu=mu tensor mu satisfies the corrected M=1 box, zero centre gap and reachability for large k, with maximal marginal of order k^-3. Conditional expectation on the first environment layer yields sum a_z eta_z, with nonnegative a_z of sum 1, at most C k^3 sites, centred lognormal eta_z of positive variance and finite fourth moment. Its variance is sigma^2 sum a_z^2; its fourth moment is at most C(sum a_z^2)^2. Paley–Zygmund and conditional Jensen imply Lp norm at least c k^-3/2. Yet xi(P,9/5)>=15/22, so the claimed corrected-box rate would be at most C k^-21/11, a strict contradiction as k grows.
checks_by_claim.counterevidence: Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 1.1(i) only supply auxiliary moments below p* wedge 2, whereas the proof on pp.18–19 chooses them near the full p*. The literal singleton statement is not declared false by a spread-out witness. Correctly bounded moments can still yield positive qualitative decay.
checks_by_claim.impact: The proof actually applies an averaging estimate outside its literal domain, and its intended full-p* quantitative rate is false. This affects a core input, so Major is retained despite a bounded repair. It is not a counterexample to the qualitative local limit conclusion.
checks_by_claim.repair_limit: Correct the box and bridge hypotheses, choose p<q<min(p*,2), and replace the full-p* rate with xi_q=min((q-1)/(q+1),(q-p)/q)*(1-(1+2/d)/q)>0. The local exponent calculation is checked; the qualitative route remains conditional on its retained external and bridge inputs.

Of 90 return paths, 15 have each event and 6 have both, giving ratio 1+7/(30delta), unbounded. A separate positive witness uses lambda=(log 2,0,0), drift 3/13, n=26ell, x=0,y=-6ell e1, s=n/2,t=n, f=4^(-X_s^1),g=1. It satisfies the printed x-y-nm=0 condition and reachability. Each tilted step has E[4^(-Delta X^1)]=1, so the denominator is 1; bridge symmetry gives E X_s^1=-3ell and Jensen gives a ratio at least 64^ell.
checks_by_claim.counterevidence: Actual Boltzmann factors are nonnegative and p.16 chooses the correct drift (b-a)/n. Thus these examples do not refute the correctly directed positive comparison used by the core proof.

checks_by_claim.verification: Use d=1 iid Bernoulli disorder with P(omega=1)=1/4 and beta=log 64. The environment is nonconstant and has every required exponential moment. Subadditivity at theta=1/2 yields E sqrt(W_n)<=(11/sqrt(134))^n; Markov and Borel–Cantelli give strong disorder. For epsilon>0 choose L with sup P_L<epsilon/2 and delta=(epsilon/2)exp(-beta L). At any block start, at most 1/delta endpoint atoms have mass above delta. Requiring zero disorder on their finite L-step tubes has conditional probability at least a uniform q_epsilon>0. Unnormalised weights are at least 1, so the denominator is at least 1. Heavy starting atoms contribute at most sup P_L and the remaining atoms at most exp(beta L)delta to any endpoint. Hence the maximum endpoint mass, and its subsequent unweighted-step maximum, are at most epsilon. Iterated conditional probabilities on disjoint blocks bound avoidance by (1-q_epsilon)^N; no unconditional independence is assumed. This happens infinitely often, and epsilon=1/j gives liminf max=0 almost surely.
checks_by_claim.counterevidence: The main weak-disorder proof uses B(i), not B(ii).
checks_by_claim.impact: The stated background strong-disorder liminf is false under all its printed assumptions; grade Minor concerns its actual background use, not ease of repair.
checks_by_claim.repair_limit: Remove the false liminf assertion. A limsup substitute needs its own correctly stated theorem and assumptions; no universal replacement is claimed.
